criteria.evidence: The article follows the brief's Mode B angle exactly: deep, respectful explanation (etymology, two-part structure, regional variation, movement symbolism) anchored in Wildcat's actual Chiang Mai camp, framed for curious travelers and beginners rather than hardcore fight fans. Matches serp-wai-kru-ram-muay.json's identified gap (no competitor combines depth with real camp grounding and beginner-friendly framing).

Each H2/H3 opens with its answer before elaborating, e.g. 'A kru is more than a coach' before explaining lineage, 'The ceremony has two distinct halves' before detailing them, 'Do all Muay Thai fighters have their own ram muay? Largely, yes' before the historical detail.

Opens on a lived scene (student kneeling at the ring), not a definition, matching patte-ecrite.md's rhythm rule. First person Meaw used where her direct experience is relevant (intro, closing quote). Brand written 'Wildcat' throughout, no warrior/hardcore register, CTA is warm and proportionate ('Try your first class', not pressuring). Names a limit explicitly ('Nobody here expects a student who isn't Buddhist... to treat the wai kru as worship').

Keywords use the spec's natural_form column throughout: 'wai kru ram muay', 'the wai in muay thai', 'the wai kru dance', 'sealing the ring', 'the movements of the wai kru', 'ram muay music', 'the music that plays during wai kru ram muay', 'becoming a certified kru'. No raw query stuffing (e.g. never 'wai kru dance muay thai Chiang Mai' as a phrase).

The two spec claims flagged 'to_confirm' (regional styles, Buddhist/religious framing) are now backed by real fetched sources (Wikipedia Wai khru ram muay, Wikipedia Muay Thai 20th century section, Evolve MMA) per {slug}.sources.json, with inline attribution.
